newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico ruling party dealt blow in state election.
newsitem.headline: Mexico ruling party dealt blow in state election.

text.p: Mexico's left dealt a heavy blow to President Ernesto Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), possibly winning 13 towns in a weekend state election, official results showed on Monday.
Sunday's vote in the rural state of Morelos south of Mexico City was a key test for the PRI ahead of congressional and governors' elections in July.
Zedillo's party had previously dominated the state's political map, holding 32 of the 33 town halls and a big majority in the state congress.

But the state electoral commission said the 860,000 registered voters now looked set to give victory in at least 13 towns to the left-leaning Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD, against 17 for the PRI.
Adding to the PRI's distress, the state capital Cuernavaca appeared to have fallen to the conservative National Action Party (PAN), which previously had no mayors in Morelos.
The PAN was ahead in two other cities -- Miacatlan and Emiliano Zapata -- which party leaders said would put PAN mayors in charge of 55 percent of the state's population.
The PRD was ahead in Cuautla, the second-largest city in the state.
In voting in 18 state legislative districts, the PRD was ahead in eight districts, the PRI seven and the PAN three, according to the two opposition parties.
There are a total of 30 seats in those 18 districts, and the PRD claimed it could end up with a majority of those seats. In any event, the PRI almost certainly would lose its absolute majority.

In Cuernavaca, which accounts for 48 percent of the state population, the PAN won 31.9 percent of the vote against 30.9 percent for the PRI and 21.3 percent for the PRD with 76 percent of polling stations reporting, the State Electoral Institute said.
"It was a historic journey for the PAN in Morelos," Adrian Rivera, president of the PAN state committee, told reporters.
But the performance of the PRD, whose election results have been overshadowed by the PAN and the PRI in other recent votes, was especially notable in Morelos.

PRD voters gave the party a stunning 64.2 percent in the town of Tepoztlan, where the PRI mayor sparked violent protests in 1995 by backing a controversial development including a golf club and industrial park. The plan was seen as out of synch with the needs of the largely poor population.
The PRI trailed with 24 percent and the PAN had a paltry 1 percent with all voting stations reporting.
In Cuautla, the PRD had won 49.5 percent the votes with 95 percent of polling stations reporting. The PRI had 28.6 percent and the PAN 7.6 percent with 95 percent.
Yet PRI leaders had not given up hope their fortunes would improve once all the votes are counted.
"The final word has not been spoken," said Juan Salgado Brito, the PRI president in Morelos.
The PRI governor of Morelos, Jorge Carrillo Olea, also warned that the results "are only preliminary" and could change.

Despite fears of violence, the elections in Morelos took place without major incident, although TV station Azteca reported late on Sunday that gunmen had been spotted driving around one town threatening voters from a car.
Late on Thursday, unknown assailants threw paint thinner in the face and broke the nose of the ruling PRI's mayoral candidate for the city of Cuernavaca.
Voters gave Zedillo's PRI a tough time in the polls in 1995 and 1996, punishing it for the country's dire economic crisis and numerous corruption scandals.
Under an aggressive new national leader, Humberto Roque Villanueva, the PRI had hoped for better times in Morelos.
But analysts said the negative publicity surrounding Gov. Carrillo had hurt the party.

Carrillo was accused by the New York Times of links to drug traffickers, a charge he denied. Carrillo's government also suffered from citizen protests against a wave of kidnappings in the state. Some victims alleged state police were involved in the crimes.
